macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise after weak jobs report
items.summary: The S&P 500 gained 0.75% to 7,724, the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19%, and the Dow advanced 0.49% after a weaker-than-expected September payrolls report reduced expectations for another near-term Federal Reserve rate hike. The VIX fell about 6%, while the 10-year Treasury yield remained near 5.28%.[1]

items.title: Fed rate-hike expectations ease
items.summary: Markets lowered expectations for an October Federal Reserve rate increase after September payroll growth came in at 29,000, well below the 90,000 forecast, while unemployment rose to 4.2%.[2]

items.title: Core PCE inflation comes in softer than expected
items.summary: August core PCE inflation rose 0.2% month over month, contributing to fading expectations of an October Fed hike and supporting technology stocks.[1]

items.title: Bond yields remain elevated despite weaker economic data
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield held around 5.28%–5.30%, keeping bond-market volatility central to equity trading even as weaker payrolls and cooler inflation reduced rate-hike expectations.[1][2]

items.title: Nike shares fall after weaker revenue outlook
items.summary: Nike shares dropped more than 8% after the company projected a high-single-digit percentage decline in fiscal 2027 revenue, significantly worse than analysts’ expected decline of about 2%. The company also said job cuts will begin next year.[2]

items.title: Micron signals tighter memory-chip market
items.summary: Micron reported strong quarterly results and said memory-chip supply and demand conditions are expected to remain considerably tighter over the next two fiscal years, supporting semiconductor stocks.[2]

items.title: Nvidia expands AWS GPU deployment
items.summary: Nvidia said Amazon Web Services was deploying an additional 2 million GPUs beginning in the current quarter through fiscal Q2 2029, underscoring continued strength in artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand.[2]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin briefly tops $87,000 before retreating
items.summary: Bitcoin rose above $87,000 intraday but closed near $84,510.80. Crypto futures liquidations reached about $291 million, with long positions accounting for most of the losses.

items.title: Blast plans to wind down Ethereum layer-2 network
items.summary: Blast reportedly plans to shut down its Ethereum layer-2 network after operating costs exceeded revenue, marking a significant retrenchment among scaling projects.

items.title: SEC approves leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETPs
items.summary: U.S. regulators approved 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ether exchange-traded products, although trading had not yet begun at the time of reporting.

items.title: Bitget hack linked to North Korea
items.summary: Coverage linked the reported $387 million Bitget hack to North Korean actors, while investigators are using artificial-intelligence tools to trace the stolen funds.

items.title: U.S. regulators signal additional crypto rules
items.summary: The SEC chair said additional cryptocurrency regulatory proposals are forthcoming. Separately, a market regulator is considering easing rules governing crypto holdings by funds and investment advisers.

items.title: Community banks sue over crypto trust charters
items.summary: A banking group filed a lawsuit challenging regulators’ approach to granting trust charters to cryptocurrency firms, escalating tensions over the treatment of crypto companies in the banking system.

items.title: BNY and Kraken parent reportedly discuss infrastructure partnership
items.summary: BNY Mellon and Payward, the parent company of Kraken, are reportedly exploring an infrastructure partnership as traditional financial institutions expand crypto-related services.

items.title: Bitcoin mining difficulty slips after September increase
items.summary: Bitcoin mining difficulty fell 0.03% to approximately 132.72 trillion in the latest adjustment, while estimated network hashrate stood near 986.07 exahashes per second.

items.title: Aave Labs proposes Cayman foundation for protocol intellectual property
items.summary: Aave Labs proposed creating a Cayman Islands foundation to hold Aave intellectual property, a move that could affect the protocol’s governance and organizational structure.

items.title: NEAR Intents reports strongest monthly fee revenue of 2026
items.summary: NEAR Intents reported its highest monthly fee revenue of the year, highlighting increased activity around the protocol’s cross-chain transaction and intent-based infrastructure.

items.title: India orders removal of Bitchat from Apple’s App Store
items.summary: Indian authorities ordered Apple to remove the Bitchat messaging application, which was also unavailable on Google Play in the country.

items.title: Fiserv launches Solana settlement infrastructure
items.summary: Fiserv reportedly launched settlement infrastructure built on Solana, adding to the growing use of public blockchains by established financial-services companies.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day reportedly sets Steam record
items.summary: The Xbox prequel reportedly delivered a strong first-day performance on Steam, with attention also focused on how it runs on Xbox Series S.

items.title: Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance expansion showcased
items.summary: Capcom presented new aerial environments, monsters and the Boost Bracer combat mechanic for the upcoming Monster Hunter Wilds expansion at Tokyo Game Show 2026.

items.title: Ubisoft unveils March of the Giants MOBA
items.summary: Ubisoft reportedly announced March of the Giants, a multiplayer online battle arena built around commanding armies rather than controlling individual heroes.

items.title: Aion 2 reaches major early-access milestones
items.summary: The MMORPG reportedly topped Steam’s Global Top Sellers chart during advanced access, reached 171,530 concurrent players and ranked first in eight countries.

items.title: AOC announces 1,050Hz esports monitor
items.summary: AOC announced the AGON PRO AGP257FT, a Full HD gaming monitor capable of an overclocked 1,050Hz refresh rate aimed at competitive players.

items.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2026 voting opens
items.summary: Public voting for the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards has opened, allowing players to select winners across major game and industry categories.

items.title: Ken Kutaragi warns of stagnation in game content
items.summary: PlayStation creator Ken Kutaragi described the industry as being at a major turning point, arguing that advances in technology and production scale have not been matched by equally innovative game ideas.

items.title: Sony Pictures reportedly wins Battlefield film rights
items.summary: Sony Pictures reportedly won the bidding for a Battlefield film adaptation, with Christopher McQuarrie attached to direct and Michael B. Jordan attached to star; production has not begun.
